learning_outcomes.text: Students can describe the three-dimensional motion of point masses and rigid bodies using vector calculus.

They can apply the impulse and angular momentum theorems and derive the equations of motion for planar movements of point masses and rigid bodies. For simple systems, they are also able to derive the solution.
They have knowledge of the relative motion of point masses and can interpret the motion in the absolute and relative systems.
They can derive the components of the mass moment of inertia matrix for different bodies and have knowledge of principal moments of inertia and principal axes of inertia.
They can independently apply the energy theorem for any three-dimensional motions of point masses and rigid bodies and evaluate the law of conservation of energy for purely conservative loads.
They know Euler's gyroscope equations and can solve them for simple problems.
Students acquire technical and methodological competencies for dealing with dynamic loads on rigid bodies.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics of point masses and rigid bodies
Kinetics of rigid bodies in inertial and relative systems
